proposals.hypothesis: Li5Al(SiO4)2 is a Li-rich, wide-gap oxide built on non-reducible Al3+ and Si4+ centers. Its high Li content should keep it ion-conducting in a thin interlayer, and it should resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl and remain oxidatively stable near 4 V against LiCoO2. It avoids the reducible transition metals of the Ti, Zr-free and Nb/Ta candidates.
proposals.motivation: The earlier Li3AlSiO5 silicate hypothesis proposed a non-reducible Al/Si Li-rich interlayer. No penalty was reported, so this closely related Al-silicate is the best available analogue in the candidate list.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium-ion conductor that is chemically compatible with both the sulfide electrolyte and the LiCoO2 surface. Its phosphate framework is oxidatively robust near 4 V, so it should suppress interfacial decomposition and electron transfer while staying a thin, ion-conducting buffer layer.

Li3BO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium-ion conductor with an oxidatively robust borate framework near 4 V. Compared with the phosphate tested earlier, it is a different chemical family that may react less with the sulfide electrolyte and the LiCoO2 surface, and it keeps the buffer thin and ion-conducting.
proposal.motivation: The earlier Li3PO4 evaluation tested an oxide buffer for the sulfide/LiCoO2 interface. Its penalty was not reported, so I am testing a different oxide family that meets the insulation and band-gap requirements.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium-ion conductor with a Li-rich antifluorite framework. Its high Li content and lack of a reducible polyanion should make it chemically gentle toward the sulfide electrolyte, and it is a different oxide family from the phosphate and borate buffers already tested. It may limit interfacial electron transfer and decomposition near 4 V, though its oxidative stability there is a concern to check.
proposal.motivation: The Li3PO4 and Li3BO3 evaluations both tested Li-rich oxide buffers. Their penalties were not reported, so I am exploring a different oxide family with a similar Li-rich, insulating character.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap (~7 eV), electronically insulating lithium-ion conductor with a highly oxidation-resistant fluoride anion, so it should remain stable near 4 V against LiCoO2. Its Li-rich, low-polarizability ionic lattice is thermodynamically unreactive toward Li6PS5Cl, which should limit sulfide oxidation and interfacial electron transfer. It is a fluoride family distinct from the oxide buffers tried so far.
proposal.motivation: The earlier evaluations tested Li-rich oxide buffers (phosphate, borate, oxide), and their penalties were not reported. I am exploring a different, fluoride-based insulating buffer that meets the band-gap and insulation requirements.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3AlSiO5 is a Li-rich, wide-gap oxide built from non-reducible Al3+ and Si4+ cations, so it should resist reduction by the sulfide electrolyte and remain oxidatively stable near 4 V on LiCoO2. Its silicate framework is a different family from the phosphate, borate, oxide and fluoride buffers already proposed, and its Li content should keep it ion-conducting in a thin interlayer.
proposal.motivation: The earlier evaluations covered phosphate, borate, simple oxide and fluoride buffers, and their penalties were not reported. This silicate candidate is a new chemical family that still meets the insulation and band-gap requirements.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3Al(BO3)2 is a Li-rich, wide-gap borate built on non-reducible Al3+ and B3+ centers. It should resist reduction by the sulfide electrolyte and stay oxidatively stable near 4 V against LiCoO2. Its ionic lattice with Al3+ rather than a reducible transition metal should limit interfacial electron transfer, and it can act as a thin ion-conducting interlayer.
proposal.motivation: Earlier evaluations covered phosphate, borate, simple oxide, fluoride and silicate buffers, and none reported a penalty. This aluminum borate is a distinct compound, so I am testing it to see whether the Al-stabilized borate framework gives a lower interfacial penalty than the simpler Li-rich oxides.

proposal.hypothesis: LiCaAlF6 is a Li-containing fluoride with wide-gap, electronically insulating character. Fluoride anions are highly oxidation-resistant near 4 V against LiCoO2, and the Ca2+/Al3+ cations are non-reducible, so the lattice should resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl. It is a mixed-metal fluoride that keeps the fluoride buffer idea while adding Li-ion conduction pathways in a thin interlayer.
proposal.motivation: The earlier LiF-based fluoride buffer hypothesis suggested that a fluoride interlayer could limit sulfide oxidation and electron transfer. No penalty was reported for it, so this is a closely related fluoride candidate that is available in the list.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2SiF6 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-ion conductor. Its fluoride anions resist oxidation near 4 V against LiCoO2, and the Si4+ cation is non-reducible, so the lattice should resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl. It is a fluoride buffer that avoids the easily oxidized halides (Br-, Cl-) and reducible Ti4+ of the other halide candidates.
proposal.motivation: The earlier LiF hypothesis proposed a fluoride interlayer to limit sulfide oxidation and interfacial electron transfer. The earlier evaluations recorded no penalty values, so I am testing a fluoride with a non-reducible cation from the available list.

proposal.hypothesis: LiZr2(PO4)3 is a wide-gap NASICON phosphate with Zr4+ centers that are very hard to reduce, so it should resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl. Its phosphate framework is oxidatively robust near 4 V against LiCoO2, and it can act as a thin Li-ion-conducting, electronically insulating interlayer.
